correctness.rationale: Exact Loewner-order averaging reduces arbitrary positive diagonal scales to a one-parameter family. Explicit 3x3 eigenvalue formulas give the optimal parameter and its two branches. The bound is established by strict analytic inequalities in three positive parameter regions: direct s<=3a, a positive completed square, and a positive difference-of-squares identity; the near-boundary family gives exact supremum 3/2. The standalone SymPy verifier replayed 6829 symbolic, exact and finite randomized checks; finite checks are not used as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The research claim is the sharp universal 3/2 worst-case cost of Jacobi relative to optimal diagonal scaling on the 2-parameter positive isosceles 3x3 SPD family, and its unattained asymptotic witness. Pointwise optimal diagonal scaling of all 3x3 SPD matrices, including the exact optimizer used in proof, is acknowledged prior art (Kolotilina 2006). None of the inspected full-text portions, general modern preconditioning papers, or actual semantic searches states or dominates this sharp relative ratio. Its proof requires three nontrivial global positivity certificates. Residual specialist precedence risk exists.
residual_risks: An earlier sharp 3/2 isosceles-family gap may occur in a less easily indexed specialist source or unchecked portion of the full 2006 study; if so novelty fails.

value.rationale: The family is a canonical two-equal-correlation SPD benchmark for matrix conditioning and cheap Jacobi scaling. The new exact 3/2 worst-case loss tightens the classic general n-factor comparison, identifies strict nonattainment, and gives an explicit nearly singular witness. This is a motivated quantitative performance limitation rather than a routine pointwise diagonal-scaling recomputation.
